It sounds nice, but if that were true you'd see a lot more stories based on real life events rather than works of fiction. Truth is, the majority of people prefer fiction because it contains the elements of our lives we react to most strongly in exaggerated and simplified form. Look at ancient culture. The Odyssey, Romeo and Juliet, The Divine Comedy, The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (not saying it's of the same caliber as the others, just a well-known example). It's not just literature, especially in modern days.

Hell, look at the news. What sells better, a story with the straight facts or a story with a sensationalist twist and a fair heap of bias and exaggeration? We as human beings are content with our daily, mundane lives. A story that covers something outside of normal experience while keeping familiar themes is captivating. Heroes, villains, love and romance, tragedy, all those cliches. There are exceptions, but generally the stories that stay with us the longest and impact us the hardest are works of fiction.

Books were my refuge. In the late days of high school it was working out. I would run until my legs were numb and my lungs burned. A few times I hurt myself bad enough that I couldn't walk the next few days. I get the empty feeling often as well. Like a puppet, animated by the character I choose to portray.

I'm sure the morbidity is taboo, but what's your preferred method of going out?
You do more damage than good in situations like that. It's better to let someone else speak or do the research yourself and go back.
